question: With new US pennies no longer minted, cash totals get rounded to the nearest five cents. Since most prices end in 99, who gains?
options: Shops, by about a cent a sale
Neither side, to a fraction of a cent
Shoppers, by about a cent a sale
answer: Neither side, to a fraction of a cent. Only the total is rounded, and sales tax and mixed baskets scatter its last digit almost evenly. In nearly 200,000 real convenience-store sales, Whaples found shoppers gained about a cent per 40 transactions; a 2025 Richmond Fed estimate put the national cost near $6 million a year.
move: Check which number actually gets rounded before counting who loses.
trap: Rounding each 99-cent tag up, as if items were paid one by one.
